nodes.name: Microscale HEA Array Preparation
nodes.procedure: Initially, a high-throughput printing workstation is used to print uniformly mixed precursor solutions onto glassy carbon (GC) substrate, generating an array of microscale HEA precursors with different compositions. Subsequently, the HEA precursor array is placed in a carbon heater and efficiently transformed into solid solution HEAs using pulse high-temperature heating technique (Ar, 0.55 s, 2023 K, 5 pulses).

nodes.name: Practical HEA@CNFs Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The top three ranked element combinations are selected and loaded onto CO2-activated carbon nanofibers (CNFs) using the same pulse high-temperature preparation process to synthesize practical electrocatalysts (HEAs@CNFs).

nodes.description: High-throughput screening of 70 HEA combinations using SECCM for ORR activity
nodes.source_text: The tip sequentially contacts the microscale HEAs in the array... for linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) measurement. In the SECCM setup... we employ a three-electrode system with Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) and a graphite rod... electrolyte solution (0.1 M HClO4). Among the 70 sets of HEA combinations, the top three combinations... are FeNiCuCoPt (C2), FeNiCoSnPt (C4), and FeNiCuSnPt (D6).

nodes.description: ORR performance evaluation using Rotating Ring-Disk Electrode (RRDE) in acidic media
nodes.source_text: The ORR performance of HEAs@CNFs is evaluated using a rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) in oxygen saturated 0.1 M HClO4... LSV curves... at 1600 RPM, with E1/2 of 0.892/0.869/0.866/0.856 V... tafel curves... slopes of 77/98/113/131 mV dec-1... MA of three HEAs@CNFs are 1.32 A mgPt-1... which are 11/7/5 times that of Pt/C (0.12 A mgPt-1)... After 10,000 cycles... E1/2... shifts negatively by only 10 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM confirms a dense surface structure for the microscale HEAs and comparable loading densities for the CNF-supported catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images and EDS imaging respectively show the dense surface structure ... nanoparticles of different HEAs have comparable loading densities (Figures 3b and S19-20).

properties.label: b
properties.description: Micrograph showing nanofibers decorated with small nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of elements without phase segregation and confirms complete decomposition of precursor salts (Cl not detected).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS imaging respectively show the ... uniform distribution of elements (i.e., no phase segregation) ... element analysis reveals complete decomposition of the precursor metal chloride salts (Figure S8; Cl element not detected).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm a single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) structure for both microscale and CNF-supported HEAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirm the formation of single-phase (face-centered cubic, FCC) alloys (Figure S9) ... XRD patterns reveal that all three HEAs have FCC crystal structure without phase separation (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-throughput screening using a three-electrode SECCM setup identified FeNiCuCoPt as the top-performing combination based on relative current density (j_relative).
nodes.evidence_snippet: SECCM-based rapid high-throughput measurement, their intrinsic ORR activity is evaluated, leading to the top three ranked element combinations ... top three combinations ... are FeNiCuCoPt (C2), FeNiCoSnPt (C4), and FeNiCuSnPt (D6).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images provided average nanoparticle sizes: FeNiCuCoPt (7.8 nm), FeNiCoSnPt (8.1 nm), and FeNiCuSnPt (6.1 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images (Figures 3c and S20) show that the nanoparticles ... have similar sizes (FeNiCuCoPt: 7.8 ± 1.7 nm / FeNiCoSnPt: 8.1 ± 1.6 nm / FeNiCuSnPt: 6.1 ± 1.1 nm).

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing nanoparticles dispersed on a fiber-like substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM identified lattice spacings of 2.15, 2.14, and 2.13 Å corresponding to the (111) plane of the FCC structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images (Figures 3d and S20) give characteristic lattice spacings (2.15/2.14/2.13 Å) corresponding to the position of the characteristic peak of the (111) plane in the XRD patterns.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirmed that element concentrations in HEAs@CNFs are consistent with the microscale HEAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) analysis confirm consistent element concentrations between HEAs@CNFs and microscale HEAs (Figure S21).

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV showed FeNiCuCoPt@CNFs has the highest E1/2 (0.892 V) and MA (1.32 A/mg_Pt). Stability test showed 10 mV negative shift after 10,000 cycles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: LSV curves of three HEAs@CNFs and commercial Pt/C at 1600 RPM, with E1/2 of 0.892/0.869/0.866/0.856 V... After 10,000 cycles of LSV, the E1/2 of the highest activity FeNiCuCoPt@CNFs shifts negatively by only 10 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping confirm the uniform spatial distribution of elements within the HEA nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM images and EDS mapping show the uniform spatial distribution of elements in the nanoparticles of three HEAs (Figures 3e and S20).

properties.description: Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy mapping showing elemental distribution in nanoparticles.
High-angle annular dark-field imaging showing mass-thickness contrast of the particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV was used to determine the non-Faradaic charging current (i_charging), which correlates linearly with ECSA (R=0.99). FeNiCuCoPt@CNFs showed the highest peak potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA of different HEAs... is highly linearly correlated with the non-Faradaic charging current (i_charging) with a correlation coefficient of up to 0.99... CV curves of stationary RRDE indicate that FeNiCuCoPt@CNFs exhibits the highest peak potential.

nodes.characterization_summary: RRDE measurements confirmed a 4-electron transfer process for the ORR on the three HEA catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The generation-collection mode of RRDE and fitting based on the Koutecky-Levich equation show that the ORR of three HEAs@CNFs involves 4e− transfer process.
